The ending is a visarga that became स् by the join, not a stand-alone स्.
Right: A visarga before त becomes स्: स्त्रियाः + तथा → स्त्रियास्तथा.
questions.explain: स्त्रियास्तथा = स्त्रियाः ('of woman') + तथा ('likewise').
questions.rule: Visarga + त → स् + त.

questions.q: A new line reads सिंहीनां क्षीरम् (सिंही = lioness), like उष्ट्रीणाम् and नागीनाम्. Whose milk is it?
optionExplain: Right: A feminine noun in -ई plus -नाम् is a genitive plural, as in उष्ट्रीणाम्: 'of she-camels'.
The ending is feminine plural, not male singular.
The -नाम् ending is plural, not singular.
Nothing in the ending marks young ones.
questions.explain: उष्ट्रीणाम् = of she-camels, नागीनाम् = of she-elephants: feminine plural 'of the females'.
questions.rule: Feminine -ई noun + नाम् / णाम् = 'of the females' (plural).
questions.teaches: A feminine noun in -ई plus -नाम् (-णाम् after र/ष) is a genitive plural: सिंही (lioness) → सिंहीनाम् 'of lionesses'.

questions.q: Verse 107 says milk is प्रायशः sweet. What does प्रायशः tell you?
optionExplain: That would need a word like सर्वदा; प्रायशः is weaker.
Right: प्रायशः means 'generally' or 'mostly'.
The verse gives sweetness as a general quality of milk.
The verse speaks of milk in general (पयः).
questions.explain: प्रायशः hedges the list: milk is generally so described.
questions.rule: प्रायशः = generally.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 107 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Taste, texture, temperature and one action word of the verse.
questions.rule: मधुरम् = sweet; स्निग्धम् = unctuous; शीतम् = cold; बल्यम् = strengthening.

questions.q: Milk is generally sweet, unctuous and ____ (type the Devanagari word for 'cold').
questions.explain: The verse says मधुरं स्निग्धं शीतम्.
questions.teaches: शीत is cold; it is the third of the general qualities named at the start.
questions.rule: शीतम् = cold.

questions.q: Which is the right split of प्रायशो मधुरं?
optionExplain: There is no word उ here.
No such word; the visarga after अ becomes ो, not आ.
Right: A visarga before a voiced sound like म becomes ो after अ: प्रायशः + मधुरं → प्रायशो मधुरं.
That would be written प्रायशमधुरं, with no ो.
questions.explain: प्रायशो मधुरं = प्रायशः ('generally') + मधुरं ('sweet').
questions.rule: अः + voiced sound → ो.

questions.q: A student wants one word from verse 107 for 'good for the intellect'. Which is it?
optionExplain: वृष्य is 'aphrodisiac'.
बल्य is 'strengthening'.
बृंहण is 'building bulk'.
Right: मेध्य = promoting intellect.
questions.explain: मेध्यम् names the intellect-promoting action.
questions.rule: मेध्य = good for the intellect.

questions.q: A new text says the fruits of a tree are प्रायशः sweet. Is a sour fruit from it a contradiction?
options: Yes, because it says all are sweet
Yes, because sweet and sour cannot share a tree
optionExplain: Right: A general statement allows exceptions.
प्रायशः does not say all.
The text only says generally.
The word प्रायशः settles it: the statement is general.
questions.explain: प्रायशः marks a general statement, as in प्रायशो मधुरम्.
questions.rule: प्रायशः = generally, so exceptions are not contradictions.
questions.teaches: When a text uses प्रायशः, read its list as the usual case, not a rule without exceptions.

questions.q: Verse 108 has no word for milk. Where does its subject come from?
optionExplain: That list names the milks, but the sentence being continued is verse 107.
Right: The sentence runs on: milk is understood.
The grammar continues verse 107; the subject is fixed.
A subject is understood from what came before, here verse 107.
questions.explain: Verses 107-109 form one sentence about milk.
questions.rule: Verse 108 continues the description of milk from verse 107.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 108 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the effects named in the verse.
questions.rule: जीवनीयम् = vitalizing; श्रमहरम् = removing fatigue; शोणितपित्तम् = bleeding disorder; सन्धानम् = uniting.

questions.q: The verse says milk destroys श्वास and ____ (type the Devanagari word for 'cough').
questions.explain: श्वासकासनिबर्हणम् = destroying dyspnoea and cough.
questions.teaches: निबर्हण means destroying; the two things destroyed are श्वास and कास.
questions.rule: श्वासकासनिबर्हणम् = destroyer of dyspnoea and cough.

questions.q: सम् + धानम् is written सन्धानम्. Which change happened?
options: म् became न् before the dental ध
optionExplain: ण् is the nasal of the retroflex group, not the dental ध.
ङ् is the nasal of the velar group.
Right: A nasal before a dental stop takes the dental nasal न्.
It changed to न्.
questions.explain: सम् + धानम् → सन्धानम्: म् → न् before ध.
questions.rule: म् before a dental stop → न्.

questions.q: A person has fatigue and cough. Which words of verse 108 apply?
optionExplain: Right: removes fatigue.
Right: destroys dyspnoea and cough.
This is about healing an injury.
शीत belongs to verse 107, not to this verse.
questions.explain: Fatigue is covered by श्रमहरम्; cough by श्वासकासनिबर्हणम्.
questions.rule: श्रमहर → fatigue; श्वासकासनिबर्हण → dyspnoea and cough.

questions.q: A new line calls a drink तापहरं. Following श्रमहरं, what does it say?
optionExplain: -हर means taking away, not causing.
The first part names what is removed.
The word says the drink removes heat.
Right: -हर is 'removing', as in श्रमहरम्.
questions.explain: श्रम + हरम् = remover of fatigue; ताप + हरम् = remover of heat.
questions.rule: Noun + हर = remover of that noun.
questions.teaches: -हर, like -घ्न and -अपह, makes a 'remover' word: the first part is what is removed.

questions.q: Verse 109 calls milk सात्म्य. Whom does it say milk is congenial to?
optionExplain: Right: सर्वप्राणभृताम् = of all living beings.
The verse says all living beings.
The verse does not limit it to children.
प्राणभृत् includes all breathing beings, not only humans.
questions.explain: सात्म्यं सर्वप्राणभृताम्: congenial to all living beings.
questions.rule: Milk is सात्म्य to all living beings.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 109 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four effects named in the verse.
questions.rule: शमनम् = pacifying; शोधनम् = purifying; तृष्णाघ्नम् = removing thirst; दीपनीयम् = stimulating digestion.

questions.q: तृष्णाघ्नम् means removing ____ (type the Devanagari word for 'thirst').
questions.explain: तृष्णाघ्नम् = तृष्णा + घ्नम्: destroyer of thirst.
questions.teaches: घ्न is the 'destroying' ending, as in दोषघ्नम् and अर्शोघ्नम् earlier; the first part, तृष्णा, is what is destroyed.
questions.rule: तृष्णाघ्नम् = removing thirst.

questions.q: Verse 109 says milk is both शमनं and शोधनं. How does the edition's note take them?
options: Two kinds of therapy: pacifying and purifying
optionExplain: They are actions of milk, not kinds of milk.
Right: शमन is palliative (calming), शोधन is evacuative (cleansing out), per the note.
They describe what milk does, not what it treats.
No animals are named in this verse.
questions.explain: शमनम् and शोधनम् are the two actions: pacifying and purifying.
questions.rule: शमन = pacify, शोधन = purify.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 109 say of milk?
options: It is congenial to all living beings
It is harmful for the wasted
optionExplain: Right: सात्म्यं सर्वप्राणभृताम्.
Right: तृष्णाघ्नम्.
Right: दीपनीयम्.
The verse says तृष्णाघ्न: it removes thirst.
The verse calls it best (श्रेष्ठम्) for the wasted and injured.
questions.explain: The verse gives positive effects only.
questions.rule: Milk: सात्म्य, शमन and शोधन, तृष्णाघ्न, दीपनीय, श्रेष्ठ in क्षीण and क्षत.

questions.q: A new text calls a decoction कासघ्नं ज्वरघ्नं च. What does it claim?
options: It is made from cough and fever
It is a food for the weak
optionExplain: -घ्न means destroying, not causing.
The first part names what is destroyed.
Right: -घ्न means destroying, as in तृष्णाघ्नम्.
Nothing in the words says this.
questions.explain: कास + घ्नम् and ज्वर + घ्नम् are destroyers of cough and fever, like तृष्णा + घ्नम्.
questions.rule: Noun + घ्न = destroying that noun.
questions.teaches: -घ्न makes a 'destroyer of X' word; you can read any new word that ends in it.

questions.q: Verse 110 lists conditions and then adds विशेषतः. Which condition does it single out?
optionExplain: Fever is in the list, but it is not the one stressed.
Burning is in the list, but it is not the one stressed.
Diarrhoea is in the list, but it is not the one stressed.
Right: श्वयथौ च विशेषतः: 'and especially in swelling'.
questions.explain: विशेषतः stands at the end of the verse, next to श्वयथौ.
questions.rule: श्वयथौ च विशेषतः = and especially in swelling.

questions.q: Match each condition named in the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Each word is a locative: 'in ...'.
questions.rule: अम्लपित्ते, अतीसारे, दाहे, श्वयथौ are all 'in' (locative) forms.

questions.q: Complete the middle of the list: अतीसारे, ____, दाहे. Type the word for 'in fever'.
questions.explain: The verse reads अतीसारे ज्वरे दाहे: diarrhoea, fever, burning. ज्वरे is the locative singular of ज्वर: 'in fever'. The whole list is in this case.
questions.teaches: A string of words ending in -ए (locative) reads 'in A, in B, in C'.
questions.rule: ज्वरे = in fever.

questions.q: Which is the right split of तथोदरे?
optionExplain: Right: आ + उ becomes ओ, so तथा + उदरे is written तथोदरे.
तथ is not a word here; the word is तथा, 'and also'.
दरे is not the word; the condition is उदर.
There is no word ओदर.
questions.explain: तथोदरे = तथा ('and also') + उदरे ('in udara').
questions.rule: आ + उ → ओ: तथा + उदरे = तथोदरे.

questions.q: श्वयथौ ends in -औ, like the dual names of verse 9. What does it mean here?
optionExplain: The meaning is 'in swelling', one condition in a list of locatives.
Right: The data gives m. loc. sg. of श्वयथु; here -औ is not the dual.
The genitive would be श्वयथोः.
The instrumental would be श्वयथुना.
questions.explain: On a word in -उ, -औ can be the locative singular; the list around it settles the case.
questions.rule: -औ is not always dual: श्वयथौ = in swelling.

questions.q: A made-up line reads कासे श्वासे ज्वरे च हितम्. What do कासे, श्वासे, ज्वरे tell you?
options: Three remedies given by the physician
Three conditions, each read as 'in ...', for which something is beneficial
Three people who give the remedy
optionExplain: The -ए words name conditions, not remedies.
Three words in a row make a list; they are not one name.
Right: Like verse 110, a run of -ए words is a list of 'in ...' conditions.
-ए here is the 'in' ending, not a person.
questions.explain: The same list pattern as verse 110: condition words in the locative, then the word for 'beneficial'.
questions.rule: Locative list + 'beneficial' = 'good in these conditions'.
questions.teaches: You can read a new list of conditions by its endings: -ए words are 'in this condition', and the word for 'beneficial' comes at the end.

questions.q: The verse ends with the word पथ्यम्. What does it say about the milk?
optionExplain: That would be अपथ्य, not पथ्यम्.
पथ्यम् is a positive word.
The word says nothing about price.
Right: पथ्य means wholesome; it completes the lists of verses 110 and 111.
questions.explain: पथ्यम् = wholesome. It is the word that all the 'in ...' conditions wait for.
questions.rule: पथ्यम् = wholesome.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words name the body parts and products in the verse.
questions.rule: योनि = female genital tract; शुक्र = semen; मूत्र = urine; पुरीष = faeces.

questions.q: पुरीषे ____: type the word that completes the phrase for faeces that are knotted and hard.
questions.explain: पुरीषे ग्रथिते: 'when the faeces are hard'. ग्रथिते is the locative singular of ग्रथित (knotted, hard). Together with पुरीषे it reads 'when the faeces are hard'.
questions.teaches: Two words in the same locative can mean 'when X is Y'.
questions.rule: ग्रथिते = when hard (said of पुरीषे).

questions.q: Which is the right split of मूत्रेष्वप्रचुरेषु?
optionExplain: Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्, so मूत्रेषु + अप्रचुरेषु is written मूत्रेष्वप्रचुरेषु.
That would give 'plentiful urine' and would not show a व्.
The व् belongs to the sandhi; मूत्रेष्व is not a word.
-षु is an ending, not a separate word.
questions.explain: मूत्रेष्वप्रचुरेषु = मूत्रेषु ('in urines') + अप्रचुरेषु ('scanty').
questions.rule: उ + अ → व् + अ: मूत्रेषु + अप्रचुरेषु = मूत्रेष्वप्रचुरेषु.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 111 itself name?
optionExplain: Right: शुक्रप्रदोषेषु.
Right: मूत्रेष्वप्रचुरेषु.
Right: पुरीषे ग्रथिते.
Fever is in verse 110, not here.
Anaemia is in verse 110, not here.
questions.explain: Verse 111 names disorders of yoni and śukra, scanty urine and hard faeces; the others are in 110.
questions.rule: 111: yoni-śukra disorders, scanty urine, hard faeces.

questions.q: A made-up line says ज्वरे शान्ते पथ्यम्. By the pattern of पुरीषे ग्रथिते, what is the best sense?
options: Wholesome in fever and in peace, two separate conditions
Wholesome when the fever has subsided
Wholesome for the one who gives the fever
optionExplain: Like पुरीषे ग्रथिते, the second word describes the first; it is not another condition.
Right: Two words in the same locative can mean 'when X has become Y'.
-ए does not mark a person.
-ए is not the 'by means of' ending.
questions.explain: Noun + describing word in the same locative = 'when the noun is so'.
questions.rule: Locative + locative describing it = 'when ...'.
questions.teaches: A pair of locatives, noun and describing word, can give a 'when' clause, so you can read a new phrase like ज्वरे शान्ते.

questions.q: What does the verse say about the use of milk (पयः) in the therapies it lists?
options: It is used everywhere, in all of them
optionExplain: Emesis is one of seven therapies listed, not the only one.
विरेचने is in the list: milk is used there too.
Right: पयः सर्वत्र युज्यते.
स्नेहने is one of seven; the verse says सर्वत्र.
questions.explain: सर्वत्र = everywhere. The verse covers all seven therapies.
questions.rule: पयः सर्वत्र युज्यते = milk is used everywhere.

questions.q: Match each therapy to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the seven therapies named in the verse.
questions.rule: नस्य = nasal therapy; अवगाह = immersion bath; वमन = emesis; विरेचन = purgation.

questions.q: The verse says पयः ____ युज्यते. Type the word that means everywhere.
questions.explain: The verse ends पयः सर्वत्र युज्यते. सर्वत्र is सर्व ('all') with the ending -त्र ('in/at'): everywhere.
questions.teaches: -त्र added to a pronoun-like word gives 'in/at', so सर्वत्र = in all places, in all cases.
questions.rule: सर्वत्र = everywhere.

questions.q: Which is the right split of नस्यालेपावगाहेषु?
optionExplain: नस्या is not the word; it is नस्य.
The words are आलेप and अवगाह; they begin with a vowel.
आलेपा and वगाह are not words.
Right: अ + आ and अ + अ both give आ; the three words are नस्य, आलेप, अवगाह.
questions.explain: नस्यालेपावगाहेषु joins three therapies: नस्य, आलेप, अवगाह.
questions.rule: अ + आ → आ and अ + अ → आ: नस्य + आलेप + अवगाह = नस्यालेपावगाह.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 112 list as therapies where milk is used?
optionExplain: Right: नस्य is first in the verse.
Right: स्नेहने च.
Right: वमनास्थापनेषु.
Fever is a condition in verse 110, not a therapy.
Anaemia is a condition in verse 110, not a therapy.
questions.explain: Verse 112 lists therapies; the conditions belong to 110 and 111.
questions.rule: 112 = therapies; 110-111 = conditions.

questions.q: A made-up line says ज्वरे कासे च, विशेषतः श्वासे. Compared with सर्वत्र in verse 112, what does विशेषतः do?
options: It picks out one item (श्वासे) for stress, instead of treating all alike
It covers all three items alike
It removes the last item from the list
It means the same as सर्वत्र
optionExplain: Right: विशेषतः stresses one item, as in verse 110; सर्वत्र covers all alike.
That is what सर्वत्र does, not विशेषतः.
It stresses an item; it does not remove it.
The two words work in opposite ways.
questions.explain: विशेषतः ('especially') singles out; सर्वत्र ('everywhere') includes all.
questions.rule: विशेषतः = singles out one; सर्वत्र = covers all.
questions.teaches: Two small words steer a list: विशेषतः stresses one item, सर्वत्र spreads the statement over all.

questions.q: Where does the speaker say the qualities of the milks will be described in full?
options: In the next verse of this chapter
In the chapter that begins with food and drink (अन्नपानादि)
Nowhere; this is the last mention
In a chapter on the origin of diseases
optionExplain: The verse says भूयः (later, again), pointing to another chapter.
Right: अन्नपानादिके ऽध्याये भूयो वक्ष्यामि: further, in that chapter.
The speaker promises to speak of them again.
The chapter is described by food and drink (अन्नपान), not diseases.
questions.explain: The promise points forward to a chapter named by अन्नपानादि.
questions.rule: अन्नपानादिके ऽध्याये = in the chapter (beginning with) food and drink.

questions.q: Match each word of the promise to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words say how the promise will be kept.
questions.rule: यथाक्रमम् = in due order; पृथक् पृथक् = separately; भूयः = further, again; अशेषतः = completely.

questions.q: भूयो ____ अशेषतः: type the verb meaning I shall describe (ending in -मि), before sandhi.
questions.explain: The verse has भूयो वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः. वक्ष्यामि is the first person singular future of √वच्: 'I shall say / describe'.
questions.teaches: -स्य- (here -ष्य- after क्) marks the future; -मि marks 'I'.
questions.rule: वक्ष्यामि = I shall describe.

questions.q: Which is the right split of वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः?
optionExplain: यशेषतः is not a word.
That would drop the अ- of अशेषतः and give a different meaning, 'from the remainder'.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्, so वक्ष्यामि + अशेषतः is written वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः.
वक्ष्याम्य is not a verb form.
questions.explain: वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः = वक्ष्यामि ('I shall describe') + अशेषतः ('completely').
questions.rule: इ + अ → य् + अ: वक्ष्यामि + अशेषतः = वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः.

questions.q: In verse 1, व्याख्यास्यामः (-मः) meant 'we shall expound'. वक्ष्यामि ends in -मि. Who speaks, and when?
options: We, a group, about the future
I, one speaker, about the future
optionExplain: 'We' ends in -मः, as in verse 1.
'He' would end in -ति and the sense is not past.
'You' would end in -सि.
Right: -मि marks 'I' and the future sense gives 'I shall'.
questions.explain: वक्ष्यामि is first person singular future: 'I shall describe'.

questions.q: A made-up teacher ends a lesson with पृथक् पृथक् भूयो वक्ष्यामि. What is he doing?
options: Promising to return to the matter and treat each part separately
Saying nothing more will be said about it
Asking his students to explain it separately
optionExplain: Right: भूयः + the future verb is a promise to come back; पृथक् पृथक् means each separately.
भूयः points to more to come.
वक्ष्यामि is 'I shall say', not a request.
The future verb looks forward, not back.
questions.explain: The pattern is the same as in verse 113: a short statement now and a fuller one promised later.
questions.rule: भूयः + future verb = a later fuller treatment.
questions.teaches: भूयः with a future verb is a promise of a later, fuller treatment of the topic.

questions.q: Verse 114 introduces a new group of plants. Which three does it name?
optionExplain: These come later, in verse 116.
Right: These are the names in स्नुह्यर्काश्मन्तकाः.
तिल्वक is not in this verse.
Only one of these three is named here.
questions.explain: The verse names exactly three plants: snuhī, arka, aśmantaka.
questions.rule: 114: स्नुही, अर्क, अश्मन्तक.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the introduction of the new group.
questions.rule: अथ = now; अपरे = other; त्रयः = three; पृथक् = separately.

questions.q: Complete the three names: स्नुही, अर्क, ____ (type the third in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The compound is स्नुह्यर्काश्मन्तकाः. The compound ends in -आः, the nominative plural: 'snuhī, arka and aśmantaka'.
questions.teaches: A compound of names in a list ends with the plural ending that covers all of them.
questions.rule: The three names are स्नुही, अर्क, अश्मन्तक.

questions.q: Which is the right split of स्नुह्यर्काश्मन्तकाः?
optionExplain: These pieces are not names.
यर्क is not a name; the name is अर्क.
Right: ई before a different vowel becomes य्, and अ + अ gives आ: three names.
अर्का is not the name; the name is अर्क and आ comes from joining it with अश्मन्तक.
questions.explain: स्नुह्यर्काश्मन्तकाः = स्नुही + अर्क + अश्मन्तकाः.
questions.rule: ई + अ → य्, अ + अ → आ: स्नुही + अर्क + अश्मन्तक.

questions.q: Which statements does verse 114 support?
options: Three other plants are being introduced
Each plant has its own action to be told
All three have exactly the same action
The actions are already listed in this verse
optionExplain: Right: अथापरे त्रयो वृक्षाः.
Right: तेषामिदं कर्म पृथक् पृथक्.
पृथक् पृथक् says the opposite: each separately.
इदं कर्म points ahead; the actions come in verse 115.
questions.explain: The verse introduces three plants and promises their separate actions; it does not state them.
questions.rule: 114 = introduction; 115 = the actions.

questions.q: A made-up line reads अथापरे द्वौ क्षारौ, तेषामिदं कर्म पृथक् पृथक्. What do you expect next?
options: A separate action for each of the two
optionExplain: पृथक् पृथक् means separately.
The line promises their action, not a list of diseases.
इदं कर्म promises that the action follows.
Right: As in verse 114, पृथक् पृथक् promises each item its own action.
questions.explain: The same frame as 114: 'now other [number] ...; their action, each separately, is this'.
questions.rule: अथापरे [number] ... तेषामिदं कर्म पृथक् पृथक् = items now, separate actions next.
questions.teaches: This opening frame tells you the next verse will give each new item its own action.

questions.q: Which is named for emesis only, with purgation not mentioned for it?
optionExplain: Right: वमने ऽश्मन्तकं विद्यात्: aśmantaka is known for emesis.
Snuhī's latex is for purgation.
Arka's latex is for emesis together with purgation.
The verse gives a use for each of the three.
questions.explain: Only aśmantaka is named for emesis without purgation; the other two involve purgation.
questions.rule: अश्मन्तक = emesis; स्नुही = purgation; अर्क = both.

questions.q: Put the three plants in the order in which verse 115 names them.
questions.explain: The verse names aśmantaka first, then snuhī, then arka.
questions.rule: Verse order: अश्मन्तक, स्नुही, अर्क.

questions.q: Complete: क्षीरमर्कस्य विज्ञेयं वमने ____ . Type the word for 'together with purgation'.
questions.explain: The verse ends वमने सविरेचने. सविरेचने = स ('with') + विरेचने ('in purgation'): emesis together with purgation.
questions.teaches: स- at the start of a word can mean 'with, together with'.
questions.rule: सविरेचने = together with purgation.

questions.q: In वमने सविरेचने, what does सविरेचने add to वमने?
optionExplain: स- means 'with', not 'instead of'.
Right: स- means 'with', so emesis comes together with purgation.
'Without' would need a word like अविरेचने or विना, not स-.
स- means 'together with', not 'after'.
questions.explain: Arka's latex is the one with the double use.
questions.rule: स + विरेचने = together with purgation.

questions.q: Which statements about verse 115 are right?
options: The latex of स्नुही is for purgation
The latex of अर्क is for emesis together with purgation
The latex of स्नुही is for emesis
The latex of अर्क is for purgation only
optionExplain: Right: वमने ऽश्मन्तकं विद्यात्.
Right: स्नुहीक्षीरं विरेचने.
Right: क्षीरमर्कस्य ... वमने सविरेचने.
The verse puts snuhī under purgation.
Arka is for emesis together with purgation, not purgation alone.
questions.explain: The three plants have three different uses: emesis, purgation, and the two together.
questions.rule: अश्मन्तक: वमन; स्नुही: विरेचन; अर्क: वमन + विरेचन.

questions.q: A made-up verse reads विरेचने कल्पकं विद्यात्. By the pattern of 115, what does it say about the plant कल्पक?
options: It is to be known as used for emesis
It is used for both therapies
It is to be known as used for purgation
optionExplain: Emesis would be वमने.
Both would need a wording like सविरेचने.
Right: 'विरेचने X विद्यात्' reads 'know X for purgation', as with snuhī in 115.
विद्यात् ('one should know') names a use; it does not forbid.
questions.explain: The pattern is: therapy in the locative, plant, and 'one should know'.
questions.rule: वमने X विद्यात् = X for emesis; विरेचने X विद्यात् = X for purgation.
questions.teaches: You can read a new plant's use from the therapy word in the locative: वमने = emesis, विरेचने = purgation.

questions.q: What do the three trees of verse 116 have in common?
optionExplain: The verse names the bark (त्वचः), not the roots.
The verse names the bark, not the fruits.
Latex was the part for snuhī and arka in verse 115, not here.
Right: येषां हिताः त्वचः: 'whose barks are beneficial'.
questions.explain: त्वचः = barks.
questions.rule: 116 trees: bark (त्वच्).

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the sense of the verse.
questions.rule: अपरान् = others; हिताः = beneficial; त्वचः = barks; आहुः = they say.

questions.q: Complete the three names: पूतीक, कृष्णगन्धा, ____ (type the third in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The verse ends तिल्वकश्च तथा तरुः. The third name is तिल्वक; तथा तरुः adds 'likewise the tree'.
questions.teaches: In a list, तथा ('likewise') introduces the last member.
questions.rule: The three bark trees are पूतीक, कृष्णगन्धा, तिल्वक.

questions.q: Which is the right split of वृक्षानाहुर्येषाम्?
optionExplain: Right: Final न् joins आहुः; the visarga after उ becomes र् before the voiced य.
नाहुः is not a word.
र्येषाम् is not a word; the र् comes from the visarga of आहुः.
The र् belongs to आहुः; the word is येषाम्.
questions.explain: वृक्षानाहुर्येषाम् = वृक्षान् + आहुः + येषाम् ('the trees; they speak; of which').
questions.rule: उः + voiced letter → उर्: आहुः + येषाम् = आहुर्येषाम्.

questions.q: Which statements fit verse 116?
options: It names Pūtīka, Kṛṣṇagandhā and Tilvaka
The barks of these trees are said to be beneficial
It says Tilvaka is used for purgation
optionExplain: Right: पूतीकः कृष्णगन्धा च तिल्वकश्च.
Right: येषां हिताः त्वचः.
That is verse 117, not this verse.
The text gives no such identification; that comes from commentators.
questions.explain: Verse 116 gives the names and the useful part (bark); the uses come in 117.
questions.rule: 116 = names + bark; 117 = uses.

questions.q: A made-up line reads इमांस्त्रीन् वृक्षानाहुर्येषां हितानि फलानि. What does it tell you about the trees?
options: Their barks are the beneficial part
Their fruits are the beneficial part
Their roots are the beneficial part
optionExplain: The made-up line says फलानि, fruits.
Right: 'येषां हिताः X' names the useful part: here fruits, in verse 116 barks.
हितानि means beneficial.
Only one part, fruits, is named.
questions.explain: The pattern येषां हिताः + part names what is useful.
questions.rule: येषां हिताः X = whose X are beneficial.
questions.teaches: The phrase 'येषां हिताः ...' names the useful part of a plant group, so you can read it for any new plant.

questions.q: Which two trees does verse 117 name for use in purgation?
optionExplain: Kṛṣṇagandhā is named for parīsarpa, swellings and piles.
Kṛṣṇagandhā is named for other conditions in this verse.
Right: विरेचने प्रयोक्तव्यः पूतीकस्तिल्वकस्तथा.
These were in verses 114-115, not in this verse.
questions.explain: Purgation goes with the first two names, Pūtīka and Tilvaka.
questions.rule: 117: पूतीक, तिल्वक = purgation.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the uses named in the verse.
questions.rule: विरेचने = in purgation; शोथेषु = in swellings; अर्शःसु = in piles; उच्यते = is said.

questions.q: Complete: कृष्णगन्धा ____ शोथेष्वर्शःषु चोच्यते. Type the first condition, the one in -ए.
questions.explain: The verse reads कृष्णगन्धा परीसर्पे शोथेष्वर्शःषु चोच्यते. परीसर्पे is the locative singular: 'in parīsarpa', a spreading skin disease.
questions.teaches: Each use of a tree is a locative: 'in this condition'.
questions.rule: परीसर्पे = in parīsarpa (spreading skin disease).

questions.q: Which is the right split of चोच्यते?
optionExplain: च्यते is not a verb form here; the verb is उच्यते.
The word is च, with short अ.
There is no verb ओच्यते.
Right: अ + उ becomes ओ, so च + उच्यते is written चोच्यते.
questions.explain: चोच्यते = च ('and') + उच्यते ('is said').
questions.rule: अ + उ → ओ: च + उच्यते = चोच्यते.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 117 itself say?
options: Pūtīka is to be used in purgation
Tilvaka is to be used in purgation
Pūtīka is for swellings and piles
optionExplain: Right: विरेचने प्रयोक्तव्यः पूतीकः.
Right: तिल्वकस्तथा.
Right: कृष्णगन्धा परीसर्पे ... उच्यते.
The verse puts Tilvaka under purgation.
Swellings and piles are listed under Kṛṣṇagandhā.
questions.explain: Purgation goes with Pūtīka and Tilvaka; parīsarpa, swellings and piles with Kṛṣṇagandhā.
questions.rule: 117: पूतीक + तिल्वक = विरेचन; कृष्णगन्धा = परीसर्प, शोथ, अर्श.

questions.q: A made-up line says क्वाथः पातव्यः, with पातव्यः built like प्रयोक्तव्यः. What does it say of the decoction?
options: It is being drunk now by someone
optionExplain: Right: The -तव्य ending, as in प्रयोक्तव्यः, means 'is to be done'.
-तव्य is not a past ending.
A negative word would be needed.
-तव्य says 'is to be', not an action in progress.
questions.explain: The ending -तव्य gives the 'is to be done' sense.
questions.rule: -तव्य = is to be (done).
questions.teaches: With the ending -तव्य you can read a new word as 'is to be ...', for example पातव्यः 'is to be drunk'.

questions.q: How does verse 118 describe the six trees at its close?
optionExplain: बृंहण was a quality of milk in verse 107, not the label of the trees.
Right: षड्वृक्षाञ्छोधनान्: the six trees are शोधन.
दीपनीय was a quality of milk in verse 109.
वृष्य was a quality of milk in verse 107.
questions.explain: The six trees are called शोधन, purifying or evacuant.
questions.rule: षड् वृक्षाः = शोधन.

questions.q: Match each condition to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are four of the conditions in the first line.
questions.rule: दद्रु = ringworm; विद्रधि = abscess; कुष्ठ = skin diseases; अलजी = pustular eruptions.

questions.q: विद्याद् ____: type the word that names the physician who should know, as the verse puts it.
questions.explain: The verse ends विद्याद्विचक्षणः. विचक्षणः is a nominative singular: the one who should know.
questions.teaches: विद्यात् ('should know') takes its subject in the nominative: विचक्षणः.
questions.rule: विचक्षणः = the discerning (physician).

questions.q: Which is the right split of षड्वृक्षाञ्छोधनान्?
optionExplain: छोधन is not a word; the छ् comes from the sandhi.
ञ्छोधन is not a word.
Right: न् + श् becomes ञ्छ्, so षड्वृक्षान् + शोधनान् is written षड्वृक्षाञ्छोधनान्.
वृक्षाञ्छोधनान् is not a word.
questions.explain: षड्वृक्षाञ्छोधनान् = षड्वृक्षान् ('six trees') + शोधनान् ('purifying').
questions.rule: न् + श → ञ् + छ: वृक्षान् + शोधनान् = वृक्षाञ्छोधनान्.

questions.q: Which conditions are listed in verse 118?
optionExplain: Right: दद्रुविद्रधिगण्डेषु.
Right: कुष्ठेष्वपि.
Right: अलजीषु च.
Parīsarpa is in verse 117.
Piles are in verse 117.
questions.explain: Verse 118 continues the list from 117; parīsarpa, swellings and piles were the first part of it.
questions.rule: 117: परीसर्प, शोथ, अर्श; 118: दद्रु, विद्रधि, गण्ड, कुष्ठ, अलजी.

questions.q: A made-up verse follows one listing a tree's uses and opens दाहे तृष्णायां च, naming no tree. Where is the tree most likely named?
options: Treat the verse as complete and meaningless
Take the subject from the verse after it
Take 'milk' as the subject by default
Look back at the previous verse for the subject, as 118 does with 117
optionExplain: The subject is understood from the verse before.
Verse 118 takes it from the verse before, 117.
The subject comes from the immediately preceding list, not from a default.
Right: A verse made only of locatives continues a list begun before it.
questions.explain: The same situation as the first line of 118, which names no tree.
questions.rule: Locatives with no subject continue the list before them.
questions.teaches: A verse of only 'in ...' words with no subject may continue the list before it.

questions.q: What kind of verse is verse 119?
options: A summary of the groups already described
The start of a new topic
A list of diseases and their cures
A prayer to end the chapter
optionExplain: Right: इत्युक्ताः = 'thus have been stated', followed by the list.
इत्युक्ताः looks back; it does not open a new topic.
The list is of drug groups, not diseases.
The verse is a list of groups already described.
questions.explain: इति + उक्ताः closes a section by recalling what has been said.
questions.rule: इत्युक्ताः = thus stated: a recap.

questions.q: Put these four groups in the order in which verse 119 names them.
questions.explain: The verse names fats, then salts, then urine, then milks.
questions.rule: Verse order: स्नेह, लवण, मूत्र, क्षीर.

questions.q: स्नेहाश्च ____ च: type the word for salts as it stands in the verse.
questions.explain: The verse reads स्नेहाश्च लवणानि च. लवणानि is the neuter nominative plural of लवण: 'salts'.
questions.teaches: Neuter a-stem nouns make the plural in -आनि: लवण → लवणानि = salts.
questions.rule: लवणानि = salts.

questions.q: What does ये दिष्टपयस्त्वचः say about the six trees?
options: Their roots and fruits have been indicated
Their milk and bark have been indicated
Their milk and bark are forbidden
Their leaves and flowers have been indicated
optionExplain: Roots and fruits belong to the other group, the phalinī and mūlinī plants.
Right: दिष्ट-पयस्-त्वचः: whose milk and bark are indicated.
दिष्ट means indicated, not forbidden.
The compound names milk and bark.
questions.explain: Three of the six trees give milk (latex), three give bark.
questions.rule: दिष्टपयस्त्वचः = whose milk and bark are indicated.

questions.q: Which items does verse 119 name in its summary?
optionExplain: Right: स्नेहाश्च.
Right: लवणानि.
Right: मूत्रम्.
Honey is not named in this verse.
Blood is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: The verse recalls fats, salts and urine among its groups; honey and blood are not in it.
questions.rule: 119 names fruit- and root-plants, fats, salts, urine, milks and six trees.

questions.q: A made-up author closes a section with इत्युक्तानि धान्यानि शिम्बयः फलानि च. What is the author doing?
options: Beginning a new list of groups
Recalling the groups already described: grains, pulses and fruits
optionExplain: इत्युक्ताः looks back, not forward.
उक्ताः means 'stated', not forbidden.
Right: इत्युक्ताः ('thus stated') is the recap marker, as in verse 119.
The line is a statement.
questions.explain: The same device as verse 119: इति + उक्ताः, then the list.
questions.rule: इत्युक्ताः + list = a summary of what has been said.
questions.teaches: इत्युक्त- often marks a closing recap, so it can help you spot the end of a section.

questions.q: In ओषधीर्नामरूपाभ्यां जानते …, who is said to know the plants by name and form?
options: Only the physicians of the council
Only the sages gathered on the Himalayan slope
Goatherds, shepherds, cowherds and other forest-dwellers
optionExplain: No physician is named in this verse.
The gods of the earlier chain do not appear here.
The sages of verses 8-10 are not the subject here.
Right: अजपाः, अविपाः, गोपाः and वनवासिनः are the knowers named.
questions.explain: The knowers are the forest folk: goatherds, shepherds, cowherds and other forest-dwellers.
questions.rule: Forest herders and dwellers know the plants by name and form.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words name the people in the verse.
questions.rule: अजपाः = goatherds; अविपाः = shepherds; गोपाः = cowherds; वनवासिनः = forest-dwellers.

questions.q: The verse says the plants are known by name and by ____ (type the Devanagari word for 'form').
questions.explain: The pair is नाम (name) and रूप (form).
questions.teaches: नामरूपाभ्याम् is a pair-compound (नाम + रूप) with the ending -आभ्याम्, 'by' two things: by name and form.
questions.rule: नामरूपाभ्याम् = by name and form (two things).

questions.q: Which is the right split of ओषधीर्नामरूपाभ्याम्?
optionExplain: Right: After ई, a visarga before a voiced letter like न becomes र्, so ओषधीः + नाम… is written ओषधीर्नाम….
र्नामरूपाभ्याम् is not a word.
The plants are in the plural, ओषधीः, ending in a visarga that turns to र्.
This would drop नाम, which the verse does name.
questions.explain: ओषधीर्नामरूपाभ्याम् = ओषधीः ('the plants') + नामरूपाभ्याम् ('by name and form').
questions.rule: ओषधीर्नाम… = ओषधीः + नाम….

questions.q: Which people does the verse itself name as knowing plants by name and form?
optionExplain: Right: named in the first line.
Right: named in the second line.
Right: named in the second line.
Physicians are not named in this verse.
Kings are not named in this verse.
questions.explain: Three herder-groups are named, plus 'other forest-dwellers' in general.
questions.rule: अजपाः, अविपाः, गोपाः (and other वनवासिनः) are the named knowers.

questions.q: A new line reads वर्णगन्धाभ्यां जानाति (वर्ण = colour, गन्ध = smell). By what is the thing known?
options: By colour and smell, two things
By colour, smell and a third thing
optionExplain: The ending covers both items, not only the first.
Right: -आभ्याम् on a pair of items means 'by' both, as in नामरूपाभ्याम्.
The ending covers both items, not only the second.
-आभ्याम् is the dual: two items, not three.
questions.explain: The same ending gives 'by two things' in any such pair.
questions.rule: X-Y-आभ्याम् = by X and Y.
questions.teaches: A pair-compound in -आभ्याम् names two means; you can read it even when the words are new.

questions.q: What does न नामज्ञानमात्रेण रूपज्ञानेन वा … deny?
options: That plants have names at all
That knowing only names, or only form, gives full knowledge of plants
That forest people know any plants
optionExplain: The verse takes names for granted; it says names are not enough.
It denies only that names or form alone are enough, not all knowledge.
Right: The verse says full understanding cannot come by names alone or by form alone.
The previous verse says they do know them; this verse says that is not the whole.
questions.explain: The verse denies that names alone or form alone give full understanding of plants.
questions.rule: Name-knowledge alone or form-knowledge alone ≠ full understanding.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the denial: what cannot be reached, and by what.
questions.rule: नामज्ञान = knowing names; रूपज्ञान = knowing form; ओषधीनाम् = of the plants; परां प्राप्तिम् = the highest attainment.

questions.q: The word meaning 'only' in नामज्ञानमात्रेण is ____ (type the Devanagari word, without the ending).
questions.explain: मात्र at the end of a compound means 'only, merely'.
questions.teaches: नामज्ञानमात्रेण = नाम-ज्ञान-मात्र + -एण: 'by the mere knowledge of names'. मात्र at the end of a compound limits the sense to just that.
questions.rule: X-मात्र = only X, merely X.

questions.q: Which is the right split of कश्चिद्वेदितुमर्हति?
optionExplain: मर्हति is not a word; the म् belongs to वेदितुम्.
चिद्वेदितुम् is not a word; कश्चित् is one word, 'anyone'.
There is no word मर्हति; the verb is अर्हति.
Right: त् before a voiced letter (व) becomes द्, and म् joins the vowel अ of अर्हति.
questions.explain: कश्चिद्वेदितुमर्हति = कश्चित् ('anyone') + वेदितुम् ('to know') + अर्हति ('is able').
questions.rule: कश्चिद्वेदितुमर्हति = कश्चित् + वेदितुम् + अर्हति.

questions.q: Which statements agree with this verse?
options: Knowing only the names of plants does not give their full understanding
Knowing only the form of plants does not give their full understanding
Knowing names of plants is worthless
Anyone who knows the form of a plant fully understands it
optionExplain: Right: नामज्ञानमात्रेण is denied as enough.
Right: रूपज्ञानेन वा is denied as enough.
The verse says names are not enough by themselves, not that they are worthless.
This is exactly what the verse denies.
questions.explain: The verse limits name-knowledge and form-knowledge; it does not condemn them.
questions.rule: Names alone and form alone are not enough; neither is called worthless.

questions.q: A new line reads न वर्णज्ञानमात्रेण कश्चिद्वेदितुमर्हति (वर्ण = colour). What does it say?
options: No one can know it by knowing only its colour
Everyone can know it by colour
Only a few can know it by colour
It can be known by colour alone
optionExplain: Right: न … मात्रेण … कश्चित् … अर्हति is the same denial as in this verse.
न makes the sentence a denial.
कश्चित् with न means 'no one', not 'few'.
मात्रेण with न says colour alone is not enough.
questions.explain: The pattern 'न … -मात्रेण … कश्चित् … अर्हति' says 'no one can … by mere …'.
questions.rule: न X-मात्रेण कश्चित् अर्हति = no one can by mere X.
questions.teaches: You can read the denial 'no one can … by mere X' for any X, using न, -मात्रेण and कश्चित्.

questions.q: In योगवित्त्वप्यरूपज्ञस्तासां तत्त्वविदुच्यते, who is called तत्त्ववित्?
options: The one who knows only the names
The one who knows the application (योग), even without knowing the form
The one who knows only the form
The one who has seen the plants in the forest
optionExplain: Names are not mentioned in this verse.
Right: योगवित् is the one called तत्त्ववित्, even if अरूपज्ञः.
The verse speaks of one who does not know the form.
Nothing in the verse speaks of seeing plants in the forest.
questions.explain: The knower of application (योगवित्) is called a knower of the true nature, even if he does not know the form.
questions.rule: योगवित् = तत्त्ववित्, even if अरूपज्ञः.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the ranking in the verse.
questions.rule: योगवित् = knower of application; अरूपज्ञः = not knowing the form; तत्त्ववित् = knower of the true nature; भिषक् = physician.

questions.q: The word meaning 'in every way' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: सर्वथा closes the second line: in every way.
questions.teaches: -था makes a word of manner: यथा (as), तथा (so), सर्वथा (in every way).
questions.rule: सर्वथा = in every way.

questions.q: Which is the right split of योगवित्त्वप्यरूपज्ञः?
optionExplain: That would lose the negative अ and say 'knowing the form', the opposite of the verse.
वित्त्वपि is not a word; योगवित् is one word.
Right: तु + अपि gives त्वपि, and इ + अ gives य (अपि + अरूप → अप्यरूप), so अरूपज्ञः keeps its negative अ.
त्वपि is not a word, and this also loses the negative अ.
questions.explain: योगवित्त्वप्यरूपज्ञः = योगवित् ('knower of application') + तु ('but') + अपि ('even') + अरूपज्ञः ('not knowing the form').
questions.rule: योगवित्त्वप्यरूपज्ञः = योगवित् + तु + अपि + अरूपज्ञः.

questions.q: A village healer cannot describe how a certain plant looks, but knows well how to use it. What does the verse call such a person?
options: Someone who knows nothing of the plant
A knower of the form only
A knower of the names only
A knower of its true nature (तत्त्ववित्)
optionExplain: The verse rates knowledge of application highly.
He does not know the form.
The verse does not speak of names here.
Right: योगवित्, even अरूपज्ञः, is called तत्त्ववित्.
questions.explain: Knowing the application is enough for the title तत्त्ववित्, even without the form.
questions.rule: योग known, रूप unknown → still तत्त्ववित्.

questions.q: A teacher says: 'Even a beginner who knows a herb's use is respected; किं पुनः one who knows it fully.' What does किं पुनः do?
options: It means 'how much more', pointing to a stronger case
It asks a plain question about the beginner
It cancels what was said before
optionExplain: Right: किं पुनः in this verse adds a still stronger case: the physician who knows the plants in every way.
It does not ask for an answer; it adds a stronger case.
'Therefore' is तस्मात्, not किं पुनः.
It strengthens, it does not cancel.
questions.explain: किं पुनः = 'how much more': first a case, then a stronger one.
questions.rule: A, किं पुनः B = if A, how much more B.
questions.teaches: किं पुनः lifts the reader from a modest case to a greater one, as the verse moves from योगवित् to the physician who knows everything.

questions.q: According to योगमासां तु यो विद्यात् …, who is the best of physicians?
options: One who knows only the names of the plants
One who, examining each person, knows the application suited to place and time
One who gives the same medicine to everyone
One who has seen the plants in the forest
optionExplain: The previous verses showed names are not enough.
Right: That is the knower described by यो विद्यात् … पुरुषं पुरुषं वीक्ष्य.
The verse says to examine each person.
Seeing plants is not the test in this verse.
questions.explain: The best physician examines each person and knows the application as suited to place and time.
questions.rule: भिषगुत्तमः = knows योग suited to देश and काल, after examining each person.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the whole test of the best physician.
questions.rule: योगम् = application; पुरुषं पुरुषम् = each person; वीक्ष्य = having examined; भिषगुत्तमः = best of physicians.

questions.q: The word meaning 'having examined' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: वीक्ष्य is 'having examined', from वि + √ईक्ष्.
questions.teaches: The root has a prefix (वि), so the 'having done' ending is -य, not -त्वा: वि + ईक्ष् → वीक्ष्य.
questions.rule: Prefix + root + -य = 'having …'.

questions.q: Which is the right split of विद्याद्देशकालोपपादितम्?
optionExplain: द्देशकालोपपादितम् is not a word.
पपादितम् is not a word; the word is उपपादितम्.
Right: त् before the voiced द् becomes द्, and अ + उ gives ओ (काल + उपपादितम् → कालोपपादितम्).
The verb form is विद्यात्, the 'would know' form.
questions.explain: विद्याद्देशकालोपपादितम् = विद्यात् ('he would know') + देशकाल ('place and time') + उपपादितम् ('adapted').
questions.rule: विद्याद्देशकालोपपादितम् = विद्यात् + देशकाल + उपपादितम्.

questions.q: Which does the best physician take into account, according to this verse?
optionExplain: Right: पुरुषं पुरुषं वीक्ष्य.
Right: देश.
Right: काल.
Not mentioned in the verse.
Not mentioned in the verse.
questions.explain: The verse names three things to fit the application to: person, place, time.
questions.rule: योग is fitted to the person, the place (देश) and the time (काल).

questions.q: A new line reads गृहं गृहं गच्छति. By the pattern of पुरुषं पुरुषम्, what does it mean?
options: He goes to one house twice
He goes to a very large house
He goes to each house in turn
optionExplain: The repetition spreads over many, not one place.
Repetition here does not mean 'large'.
Nothing in the pattern gives a denial.
Right: Saying a word twice, as in पुरुषं पुरुषम्, spreads it over each one: each house.
questions.explain: A word repeated, as in पुरुषं पुरुषम्, can mean 'each one in turn'.
questions.rule: X X = each X in turn.
questions.teaches: Repeating a noun can mean 'each one, one by one'; use this to read similar phrases.

questions.q: In this verse, to what is a medicine that is not known compared?
options: Poison, a weapon, fire and a thunderbolt
A forest herb and a root
optionExplain: Right: यथा विषं यथा शस्त्रं यथा ऽग्निरशनिर्यथा gives these four.
Nectar is the comparison for the well-known medicine, in the second line.
No such comparison appears in the verse.
These are plants, not comparisons in this verse.
questions.explain: The unknown medicine is compared with four dangers: poison, weapon, fire, thunderbolt.
questions.rule: अविज्ञात औषध = विष, शस्त्र, अग्नि, अशनि.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four are the dangers of the unknown medicine.
questions.rule: विषम् = poison; शस्त्रम् = weapon; अग्निः = fire; अशनिः = thunderbolt.

questions.q: The word meaning 'not (properly) known' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: अविज्ञातम् is the unknown medicine; विज्ञातम् is the known one.
questions.teaches: अ- in front of a word gives its opposite: अविज्ञात (not known) against विज्ञात (known). The second half of the verse turns on this pair.
questions.rule: अ + विज्ञात = अविज्ञात, the opposite.

questions.q: Which is the right split of तथौषधमविज्ञातम्?
optionExplain: That would be written तथौषधं विज्ञातम्, and would mean 'known'.
Right: आ + औ joins as औ (तथा + औषधम् → तथौषधम्), and अविज्ञातम् keeps its negative अ.
The word is तथा ('so'), which loses its final आ in the join.
उषधम् is not a word; it is औषधम्.
questions.explain: तथौषधमविज्ञातम् = तथा ('so') + औषधम् ('medicine') + अविज्ञातम् ('not known').
questions.rule: तथौषधमविज्ञातम् = तथा + औषधम् + अविज्ञातम्.

questions.q: Which statements fit this verse?
options: A medicine that is not known is compared to poison
A medicine that is well known is compared to nectar
A medicine that is well known is compared to fire
A medicine that is not known is compared to nectar
optionExplain: Right: यथा विषं … तथौषधमविज्ञातम्.
Right: विज्ञातममृतं यथा.
Fire is a comparison for the unknown medicine.
Nectar is for the well-known medicine.
questions.explain: The two lines are a pair: not known → dangers; well known → nectar.
questions.rule: अविज्ञात ↔ विष etc.; विज्ञात ↔ अमृत.

questions.q: A new line reads यथा विषं तथा यन्त्रमविज्ञातम् (यन्त्र = machine). What does it say?
options: A machine that is well known is like poison
Poison is like a well-known machine
A machine that is not known is like poison
A machine that is not known is like nectar
optionExplain: अ- makes it 'not known', the opposite.
The line compares the machine to poison, and says 'not known'.
Right: यथा X तथा Y = as X, so Y; अविज्ञातम् means 'not known'.
The comparison named is poison, not nectar.
questions.explain: 'यथा X तथा Y' compares Y with X, and अ- reverses 'known' into 'not known'.
questions.rule: यथा X तथा Y(अ-ज्ञात) = an unknown Y is like X.
questions.teaches: You can read a new यथा … तथा comparison, and tell known from not known by the negative अ-.

questions.q: By which three must a medicine be known, according to नामरूपगुणैस्त्रिभिः?
optionExplain: Price and season are not named.
Dose and place are not among the three.
Application (योग) is the second condition, not the third of the three.
Right: नाम, रूप and गुण are the three.
questions.explain: The three are नाम (name), रूप (form) and गुण (qualities).
questions.rule: The three: नाम, रूप, गुण.

questions.q: Put the three in the order the verse gives them.
questions.explain: नामरूपगुणैः lists name, form and qualities in this order.
questions.rule: नाम → रूप → गुण.

questions.q: The word meaning 'wrongly applied' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: दुर्युक्तम् is the second cause of harm.
questions.teaches: दुर् is a prefix meaning 'bad, wrong'; दुर्युक्त is 'badly or wrongly applied', formed from the same root √युज् (to join, apply) as युक्त.
questions.rule: दुर् + युक्त = wrongly applied.

questions.q: Which is the right split of ह्यनभिज्ञातम्?
optionExplain: Right: इ + अ joins as य, so हि + अनभिज्ञातम् is written ह्यनभिज्ञातम्, 'for … not known'.
That would be written ह्यभिज्ञातम् and would lose the negative.
नभिज्ञातम् is not a word.
यनभिज्ञातम् is not a word.
questions.explain: ह्यनभिज्ञातम् = हि ('for') + अनभिज्ञातम् ('not known').
questions.rule: ह्यनभिज्ञातम् = हि + अनभिज्ञातम्.

questions.q: According to this verse, when does a medicine lead to harm?
options: When it is not known by name, form and qualities
When it is known but wrongly applied
When it is known by all three and rightly applied
optionExplain: Right: ह्यनभिज्ञातं … त्रिभिः.
Right: विज्ञातं चापि दुर्युक्तम्.
The verse names no harm for that case.
Cost is not mentioned in the verse.
questions.explain: The verse gives two cases of harm: unknown, and known but wrongly applied.
questions.rule: Harm comes from अज्ञान or from दुर्योग.

questions.q: By the pattern of दुर्युक्तम् ('wrongly applied'), what does दुर्भाषितम् mean?
optionExplain: दुर् gives the opposite of 'well'.
Right: दुर् + a past participle gives 'badly done': भाषित is 'spoken'.
दुर् means 'badly', not 'not at all'.
The prefix gives no sense of number.
questions.explain: दुर् + past participle = 'wrongly, badly done'.
questions.rule: दुर् + participle = badly done.
questions.teaches: The prefix दुर् turns a participle into 'badly …' and helps you read new words like दुर्भाषितम्.

questions.q: According to योगादपि विषं तीक्ष्णम् …, what can happen to a poison through proper application?
options: It may become an excellent medicine
optionExplain: The verse says proper application can change this.
That is what happens to a wrongly applied medicine.
Right: उत्तमं भेषजं भवेत् says it can become an excellent medicine.
The verse says it becomes an excellent medicine.
questions.explain: Through proper application a poison may become an excellent medicine.
questions.rule: योगात् poison → medicine.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the two turns of the verse.
questions.rule: योगात् = through application; विषम् = poison; भेषजम् = medicine; संपद्यते = becomes.

questions.q: In the second line a wrongly applied medicine becomes ____ (type the Devanagari word for 'poison').
questions.explain: The second line ends with विषम्.
questions.teaches: The two lines mirror each other: line 1 turns विषम् into भेषजम्, line 2 turns भेषजम् into विषम्.
questions.rule: Line 1: poison → medicine; line 2: medicine → poison.

questions.q: Which pairing of the two lines is right?
options: Line 1: medicine becomes poison. Line 2: poison becomes medicine
Line 1: poison becomes medicine by proper application. Line 2: medicine becomes poison by wrong application
optionExplain: The two turns are in the opposite order.
Line 1 turns poison into medicine.
Line 2 turns medicine into poison.
Right: योगात् … भेषजं भवेत् is line 1; दुर्युक्तं … विषम् is line 2.
questions.explain: Line 1 turns poison into medicine through योग; line 2 turns medicine into poison through दुर्योग.
questions.rule: L1: विष → भेषज (योगात्); L2: भेषज → विष (दुर्युक्त).

questions.q: One physician uses a strong herb well and the patient recovers; another uses it wrongly and harms him. What does this show?
options: The result depends on how it is applied, not only on the substance
A strong herb is always harmful
The herb changes its name between the two
Only the form of the herb matters
optionExplain: Right: योगात् and दुर्युक्तम् make the application decide.
The verse says proper use can make even poison a medicine.
Names are not at issue in this verse.
Form is not the point of this verse.
questions.explain: The same substance can heal or harm depending on its application.
questions.rule: Result = substance + योग.

questions.q: A teacher says: 'Fire cooks food when used well and burns the house when used badly.' Which idea of the verse does this repeat?
options: The same thing helps or harms according to how it is applied
Fire is a kind of medicine
optionExplain: The teacher says fire cooks food when used well.
Right: This is the योग / दुर्योग idea, shown with fire instead of medicine.
The example is about fire in use, not medicine.
The idea is proper use, not avoidance.
questions.explain: Proper use turns a dangerous thing into a help; wrong use does the opposite.
questions.rule: Same thing, two uses: योग helps, दुर्योग harms.
questions.teaches: The turn from poison to medicine and back is a general lesson about application; you can apply it to other things.

questions.q: Who is told not to accept medicine, and from whom, in तस्मान्न भिषजा युक्तम् …?
options: A physician, from a wise patient
A wise person who desires life and health, from a physician devoid of yukti
A sick person, from any physician at all
optionExplain: The physician is the giver, not the one told.
Neither a king nor a sage appears in the verse.
Right: धीमता … जीवितारोग्यकाङ्क्षिणा is the one told; युक्तिबाह्येन भिषजा is the giver.
The verse limits this to a physician devoid of yukti.
questions.explain: The wise person who wants life and health should not accept medicine from a physician devoid of yukti.
questions.rule: Wise patient ← no medicine from a युक्तिबाह्य physician.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
pairs: by one desiring life and health
questions.explain: These words say who is advised and what is refused.
questions.rule: युक्तिबाह्येन = devoid of yukti; धीमता = by a wise person; जीवितारोग्यकाङ्क्षिणा = by one desiring life and health; भेषजम् = medicine.

questions.q: The word meaning 'therefore' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: तस्मात् opens the verse and draws the conclusion.
questions.teaches: तस्मात् is the -आत् form of तद् ('that'): 'from that', so 'for that reason'. It also appears in verse 5 (तस्माच्छक्रम्); here it draws a conclusion from verses 124-126.
questions.rule: तस्मात् = therefore.

questions.q: Both भिषजा and धीमता end in -आ. Which reading is right?
options: भिषजा = by the wise person; धीमता = by the physician
भिषजा = by the physician who gives; धीमता = by the wise person who should not accept
optionExplain: The two roles are swapped.
धीमता means 'by the wise person'.
भिषजा means 'by the physician'.
Right: युक्तं is 'administered' by the physician; आदेयम् 'to be accepted' goes with the wise person (धीमता).
questions.explain: Two instrumentals: the physician gives (भिषजा), the wise person should not accept (धीमता).
questions.rule: भिषजा = by the physician; धीमता = by the wise person.

questions.q: A person gives medicine at random, with no reasoned plan for the illness. What should a wise person who wants health do?
options: Not accept any medicine from him
Accept it, because he is a physician
Accept it, but only a little
Accept it, if it is cheap
optionExplain: Right: युक्तिबाह्येन … न … किंचिदादेयम्: no medicine at all from such a physician.
The verse refuses medicine from a physician devoid of yukti.
किंचित् here means 'any at all', so even a little is refused.
Cost is not mentioned.
questions.explain: A physician with no reasoned plan is युक्तिबाह्य; the wise take nothing from him.
questions.rule: युक्तिबाह्य physician → accept nothing.

questions.q: By the pattern of युक्तिबाह्य (outside yukti), what does शास्त्रबाह्य mean (शास्त्र = the authoritative treatise)?
options: Outside the śāstra, not following its rules
optionExplain: बाह्य means 'outside', not 'inside'.
Right: X-बाह्य means 'outside X' or 'devoid of X'.
बाह्य gives no sense of teaching.
बाह्य does not name a person.
questions.explain: X-बाह्य = outside X, devoid of X.
questions.rule: X-बाह्य = devoid of X.
questions.teaches: बाह्य at the end of a compound means 'outside or without', as in युक्तिबाह्य; use it to read new words.

questions.q: In this verse, which is the worse for the patient?
options: Indra's thunderbolt falling on the head
A medicine prescribed by a physician who knows yukti
A medicine prescribed by an ignorant person
optionExplain: The verse says it might leave something remaining.
No such medicine is spoken of here.
Right: It is said not to leave the patient with anything remaining.
No chance poison is mentioned in the verse.
questions.explain: The verse says the thunderbolt might leave something, but an ignorant person's medicine would leave nothing.
questions.rule: अज्ञमतम् औषधम् is worse than वासवाशनिः.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words set the thunderbolt against the ignorant person's medicine.
questions.rule: वासवाशनिः = Indra's thunderbolt; मूर्ध्नि = on the head; आतुरम् = the patient; अज्ञमतम् = prescribed by an ignorant one.

questions.q: वासवाशनिः means the thunderbolt of वासव, that is, of ____ (type the god's name in Devanagari).
questions.explain: वासव is a name of Indra.
questions.teaches: वासव-अशनिः joins two words: 'of Vāsava' and 'thunderbolt'. Vāsava is Indra, the god Bharadvāja approached in verse 3.
questions.rule: वासव = Indra; वासवाशनिः = Indra's thunderbolt.

questions.q: Which is the right split of कुर्यान्नत्वज्ञमतमौषधम्?
optionExplain: That would lose the negative अ and make him 'knowing'.
न्नत्व is not a word.
त्वज्ञमतम् is not a word; तु and अज्ञ… are separate words.
Right: त् + न joins as न्न, and तु + अ gives त्व (तु + अज्ञ → त्वज्ञ).
questions.explain: कुर्यान्नत्वज्ञमतमौषधम् = कुर्यात् ('would make') + न ('not') + तु ('but') + अज्ञमतम् + औषधम्.
questions.rule: कुर्यान्नत्वज्ञमतमौषधम् = कुर्यात् + न + तु + अज्ञमतम् + औषधम्.

questions.q: Which statements agree with the verse?
options: A thunderbolt on the head might leave one with something remaining
A medicine prescribed by an ignorant person would leave the patient with nothing remaining
A thunderbolt on the head never leaves anything remaining
An ignorant person's medicine is milder than a thunderbolt
optionExplain: Right: सशेषं वासवाशनिः.
Right: सशेषमातुरं कुर्यान्न ….
The verse says it might.
The verse says the opposite.
questions.explain: The verse puts the thunderbolt, which might spare something, against the ignorant person's medicine, which would not.
questions.rule: वज्र: possibly सशेष; अज्ञ की औषध: not सशेष.

questions.q: By the pattern of सशेषम् (with a remainder), what does सफलः (as in सफलो वृक्षः) mean?
optionExplain: Right: स- at the start of such a word means 'with': स + फल = with fruit.
सशेषम् is 'with a remainder', not 'without'.
स- gives 'with', not 'only'.
The pattern gives 'having', not a profession.
questions.explain: स- + noun = 'having, with that noun'.
questions.rule: सX = with X.
questions.teaches: स- joined to a noun means 'with it'; you can read words like सफल the same way.

questions.q: Verse 129 describes a giver of medicine with 'यः'. How does the sentence end in this verse?
options: It ends by praising the giver
It does not end here; the main statement about him comes in the next verse
It ends by saying what the medicine cures
It ends by naming the patient
optionExplain: No praise appears; the sentence is unfinished.
Right: The यः clause waits for its तस्य in verse 130.
No cure is mentioned; the clause only describes the giver and the patient.
The patient is described, not named.
questions.explain: This is a relative clause (यः …) whose main statement is in verse 130.
questions.rule: यः … प्रयच्छति is completed in verse 130.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four describe the patient.
questions.rule: दुःखिताय = to the suffering; शयानाय = to the bedridden; श्रद्दधानाय = to the trusting; रोगिणे = to the sick person.

questions.q: The word meaning 'without knowing' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: अविज्ञाय means 'without knowing (having not known)'.
questions.teaches: It ends in -य, like वीक्ष्य in verse 123: the 'having done' ending after a prefix (वि). Here it is negated with अ-, an irregular but usual form in this text.
questions.rule: अविज्ञाय = without knowing.

questions.q: What does the compound प्राज्ञमानी mean?
optionExplain: -मानी means 'thinking himself', not 'being'.
The compound has no sense of being honoured.
Right: प्राज्ञ ('wise') + -मानी ('thinking himself') describes the giver.
The compound has no sense of teaching.
questions.explain: प्राज्ञमानी = प्राज्ञ + मानी: one who considers himself wise (and so need not be).
questions.rule: प्राज्ञमानी = thinking himself wise.

questions.q: Which describe the patient in this verse?
optionExplain: Right: दुःखिताय.
Right: शयानाय.
Right: श्रद्दधानाय.
Wealth is not mentioned.
This describes the giver, not the patient.
questions.explain: The patient is suffering, bedridden and trusting; 'thinking himself wise' describes the giver.
questions.rule: Patient: दुःखित, शयान, श्रद्दधान; giver: प्राज्ञमानी.

questions.q: A verse begins यो ऽविद्वान् चिकित्सति … and stops. Following verse 129, what should you expect?
options: A new topic unrelated to the clause
A following verse that finishes the sentence (for example with तस्य, 'of him')
optionExplain: A यः clause alone has no main statement.
The clause is completed, not dropped.
The clause shows only that the sentence goes on.
Right: A यः clause waits for its main statement, as in verses 129 and 130.
questions.explain: A relative clause (यः …) is finished by a main clause, which may come in the next verse.
questions.rule: यः … → तस्य … completes the sentence.
questions.teaches: When a verse has a यः clause with no main statement, look to the next verse for the answer (तस्य …).

questions.q: In verse 129, यः introduces the man who gives medicine without knowing it. Which word of verse 130 picks that 'he' up again?
optionExplain: Right: तस्य means 'of him' and refers back to the giver.
नरः is the man who talks with him, a different person.
स्यात् is a verb ('would be'), not a person.
अपि means 'even'; it names no one.
questions.explain: तस्य picks up यः: the whole of 129-130 is one sentence.
questions.rule: यः in 129 is answered by तस्य in 130.

questions.q: Match each description of the giver to its meaning.
questions.explain: All four describe the same person, the ignorant giver of medicine.
questions.rule: त्यक्तधर्म = abandoned dharma; पाप = sinful; मृत्युभूत = death itself; दुर्मति = evil-minded.

questions.q: संभाषणादपि = संभाषणात् + ____ (type the word meaning 'even' in Devanagari).
questions.explain: अपि means 'even': even from talking with him.
questions.teaches: A final त् becomes द् before a vowel: संभाषणात् + अपि is written संभाषणादपि.
questions.rule: संभाषणादपि = संभाषणात् + अपि, 'even from conversing'.

questions.q: Which is the right split of स्यात्तस्य?
optionExplain: त्तस्य is not a word.
Right: The verb स्यात् ('would be') is followed by तस्य ('of him'); त् + त् simply stand together.
Neither piece is a word here.
That would be written स्यादस्य, with द्.
questions.explain: स्यात्तस्य = स्यात् + तस्य.
questions.rule: स्यात्तस्य = स्यात् + तस्य.

questions.q: Which of these describe the bad physician of verses 129-130?
optionExplain: Right: 'sinful' describes him.
This is the man who talks with him, not the physician.
Right: 'evil-minded' describes him.
This is the act of talking, not a description of him.
Right: 'who is death itself' describes him.
questions.explain: The words in the 'of him' form describe the giver; नरः and संभाषणात् belong to the man who talks.
questions.rule: The -स्य / -तेः words describe the giver.

questions.q: A new line reads क्रूरस्य लुब्धस्य तस्य सेवनादपि नरो दुःखी स्यात्. Whom do क्रूरस्य and लुब्धस्य describe?
optionExplain: नरः has a different ending; it is the man who suffers.
सेवनात् names an act, not a person.
Right: They end like तस्य ('of him') and describe the same person.
दुःखी is the result, said of the man.
questions.explain: Describing words stand in the same form as the person they describe: -स्य ... -स्य ... तस्य.
questions.rule: Words in the same ending as तस्य describe him.
questions.teaches: You can find whom a string of describing words refers to by matching its ending to the person-word (तस्य) that closes it.

questions.q: The verse opens with the word वरम्. What does it announce?
options: A question put to the sages
A comparison: the following things are called better
optionExplain: वरम् is not a verb of command.
Nothing here is a question.
The items named are harsh things, not medicines.
Right: वरम् means 'better': what follows is preferred to something.
questions.explain: वरम् sets up a comparison: A is better (than B).
questions.rule: वरम् = better; a comparison follows.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the harsh things named in the verse.
questions.rule: आशीविषविषम् = snake's venom; ताम्रम् = copper; अयोगुडाः = iron balls; क्वथितम् = boiled, molten.

questions.q: The word for 'drunk' that goes with the venom and the copper is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: पीतम् is 'drunk'.
questions.teaches: पीतम् is a past participle in the neuter singular, so it goes with the neuter singular nouns (the venom and the copper).
questions.rule: पीतम् = drunk; it agrees with the venom and the copper.

questions.q: भक्षिता वा in the second line has a long -आ ending, though the iron balls are plural. What explains it?
options: The visarga of -आः drops before the voiced sound भ् / व्
The word is a singular feminine noun
The poet left the ending out by mistake
optionExplain: Right: -आः + a voiced consonant gives -आ: सन्तप्ताः भक्षिताः → सन्तप्ता भक्षिता.
The data reads it as masculine plural, agreeing with अयोगुडाः.
The dual of such a word would end in -औ.
This is regular sandhi, not a mistake.
questions.explain: सन्तप्ताः and भक्षिताः lose their visarga before a voiced sound, leaving -आ.
questions.rule: -आः before a voiced consonant → -आ.

questions.q: Put the three things in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The venom comes first, the copper next, the iron balls last.
questions.rule: Venom, then copper, then iron balls.

questions.q: A speaker begins a new line with वरं मौनम् (invented) and then pauses. What do you expect next?
options: Something that silence is preferred to
optionExplain: Nothing in वरम् points to a prayer.
Right: वरम् starts a comparison, so the thing that is worse still has to be named.
वरम् starts a comparison, not a list of medicines.
वरम् opens a sentence, it does not close one.
questions.explain: As in 131 → 132, वरम् leaves the 'worse' side to be supplied.
questions.rule: वरम् A ... : the worse alternative follows.
questions.teaches: When a sentence opens with वरम्, look ahead for the alternative it is being preferred to.

questions.q: Verse 131 said what is better. The word न तु at the start of 132 does what?
options: It repeats that the venom is better
It starts a new, unrelated topic
It rules out the opposite: taking food, drink or money this way is not better
It asks the patient a question
optionExplain: न तु turns to something else.
The two verses form one sentence.
Right: न तु = 'but not': the second half of the comparison.
Nothing here is a question.
questions.explain: न तु completes the comparison: A is better, but not B.
questions.rule: वरम् ... न तु = better ..., but not ....

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The three things taken, and the one they are taken from.
questions.rule: अन्नम् = food; पानम् = drink; वित्तम् = money; रोगपीडितात् = from one afflicted by disease.

questions.q: नतु = न + ____ (type the second word, meaning 'but', in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The source writes नतु as one token; it is न + तु.
questions.teaches: नतु is न ('not') + तु ('but'), the pair that finishes the comparison begun by वरम्.
questions.rule: नतु = न + तु = 'but not'.

questions.q: Which word names the person who takes the food, drink or money?
optionExplain: This is the person it was taken from (the refugee).
This is also the patient it was taken from.
This means 'of the learned': the people whose garb is copied.
Right: It is the 'by' form; the wearer of the learned man's garb is the one who took.
questions.explain: बिभ्रता (by the wearer) is the taker; the two -आत् words are the patient.
questions.rule: बिभ्रता is a 'by' form of बिभ्रत्; the -आत् words are 'from' forms.

questions.q: Which three things does the verse say are taken from the patient?
optionExplain: Right: food.
Medicine is not among the things named in this verse.
Right: drink.
Right: money.
The garb is worn by the taker, not taken from the patient.
questions.explain: Food, drink and money are taken; the garb is worn.
questions.rule: अन्नम्, पानम्, वित्तम् are what is taken.

questions.q: In a new line धनुर्बिभ्रता वीरेण शत्रुर्जितः (invented), who carries the bow?
optionExplain: Right: बिभ्रता (carrying) and वीरेण (by the hero) are both 'by' forms, so बिभ्रता describes वीरेण, as it names the taker in 132.
The enemy was defeated; he is not the carrier.
The bow is what is carried.
वीरेण names him.
questions.explain: बिभ्रता agrees with the 'by' word: whoever it describes does the carrying.
questions.rule: बिभ्रता + 'by' person = the one who carries.
questions.teaches: A describing word in the 'by' case (here बिभ्रता) agrees with the 'by' person and names the doer, as in 132.

questions.q: According to verse 133, in what should an aspiring physician make the utmost effort?
optionExplain: Verse 132 condemned taking money from the pretender's patients; no such aim is given.
Right: स्वगुणसम्पदि = in the accomplishment of his own qualities.
Nothing in the verse speaks of rivals.
No patron or king is mentioned.
questions.explain: The effort is directed at his own qualities.
questions.rule: Effort goes into स्वगुणसम्पद्, one's own qualities.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words that carry the verse.
questions.rule: भिषक् = physician; बुभूषुः = wishing to be; मतिमान् = intelligent; प्राणदः = giver of life.

questions.q: The verse says he should make the utmost ____ (type the Devanagari word for 'effort', with or without the ending).
questions.explain: प्रयत्नम् means 'effort'.
questions.teaches: प्रयत्नम् is the object of आतिष्ठेत् ('should undertake'), qualified by परम् ('utmost').
questions.rule: परं प्रयत्नम् = utmost effort.

questions.q: Which word of the verse gives the purpose 'so that'?
optionExplain: अतः means 'therefore': it points back to the reason, not forward to the purpose.
परम् means 'utmost' and qualifies the effort.
Right: यथा with स्यात् ('may be') means 'so that he may be'.
सम्पदि means 'in the perfecting'; it names the field in which the effort is made.
questions.explain: अतः gives the reason from before; यथा gives the aim that follows.
questions.rule: अतः = therefore (reason); यथा = so that (purpose).

questions.q: A student who wishes to be a physician puts all his effort into earning, none into his own qualities. Which advice of 133 does he ignore?
options: Waiting until others approve of him
Making the utmost effort at the perfection of his own qualities
optionExplain: That is not what this verse says.
Nothing like this is said here.
No approval is mentioned in this verse.
Right: That is the effort the verse asks for.
questions.explain: He ignores the verse's main advice: effort at his own qualities.
questions.rule: The aim is one's own qualities, not income.

questions.q: A new word जिजीविषुः is built like बुभूषुः. What does it most likely mean?
options: One who is afraid of life
optionExplain: Right: The wish-form ending -षु (after a doubled syllable) means 'wishing to', so जिजीविषुः = wishing to live.
Past action would not use this wish-ending.
That is the sense of प्राणदः, a different word.
Nothing in the form suggests fear.
questions.explain: बुभूषुः = wishing to be; जिजीविषुः = wishing to live.
questions.rule: Doubled syllable + -षु = 'wishing to ...'.
questions.teaches: You can read a new wish-word by comparing it with बुभूषुः.

questions.q: According to verse 134, what makes a medicine proper (युक्त)?
options: That a famous physician gives it
optionExplain: Cost is never mentioned.
Right: यदारोग्याय कल्पते = which is capable of bringing about health.
Fame plays no part in the test.
The test is its effect on health, not its taste.
questions.explain: The test is whether it conduces to health.
questions.rule: Proper medicine = the one that conduces to health.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The words of the first line.
questions.rule: तत् = that; युक्तम् = proper; आरोग्याय = for health; कल्पते = conduces.

questions.q: सः भिषजां ____, meaning he is the best of physicians (type the Devanagari word for 'best', with or without the ending).
questions.explain: श्रेष्ठः means 'the best'.
questions.teaches: श्रेष्ठः is nominative singular, agreeing with सः; the visarga becomes ओ before the voiced र् of रोगेभ्यः (श्रेष्ठो रोगेभ्यः).
questions.rule: श्रेष्ठो = श्रेष्ठः (best).

questions.q: Verse 132 mentioned someone who wears the garb of the learned. By the test in 134, which marks the best physician?
options: Wearing the garb of the learned
Taking food, drink and money from patients
optionExplain: 134 never names the garb as a test.
132 rejects this.
Right: The test of 134 is the result for the patient.
The verse's test is freeing from disease.
questions.explain: The verse's test is freeing people from disease, not the garb.
questions.rule: Best physician = he who frees from disease (the garb is not the test).

questions.q: Which statements follow from verse 134?
options: A medicine that does not conduce to health is not 'proper' by this test
The best physician is the one who frees people from diseases
A medicine is proper if it is expensive
The verse says the physician frees people by diet alone
optionExplain: Right: only the one that conduces to health is called proper.
Right: this is the verse's own statement.
Cost is not a test in the verse.
The verse does not say how.
questions.explain: Both tests are about results: health for the medicine, freedom from disease for the physician.
questions.rule: Proper medicine → health; best physician → freedom from disease.

questions.q: A new line reads तदेव शस्त्रं यद्रणे जयाय कल्पते (invented). By the same rule, what makes a weapon proper?
options: That it is made of gold
That it is lighter than others
That it conduces to victory in battle
optionExplain: The rule is about serving the end, not material.
Ownership is not the test.
Weight is not mentioned.
Right: यत् … तत् with कल्पते + 'for ...' says: that which serves the end is the proper one.
questions.explain: 'तदेव X यत् Y-आय कल्पते' = that alone is the proper X which serves Y.
questions.rule: तदेव ... यत् ... कल्पते = that alone is proper which serves the end.
questions.teaches: The pattern तदेव X यत् ...-आय कल्पते lets you read any 'that alone is proper which serves such-and-such' line.

questions.q: In verse 135, what proclaims (आख्याति) the correct application of all procedures?
optionExplain: Right: सिद्धिः is the subject of आख्याति in both lines.
Trust appears in verse 129, not as the proclaimer here.
Wealth is not mentioned in 135.
Fame is not mentioned in 135.
questions.explain: सिद्धिः is the subject: success proclaims.
questions.rule: सिद्धिः आख्याति = success proclaims.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four key words.
questions.rule: सिद्धिः = success; आख्याति = proclaims; कर्मणाम् = of procedures; भिषक्तमम् = the best physician.

questions.q: भिषक्तमम् = भिषक् + ____: type the ending that means 'most' (it makes 'best') in Devanagari.
questions.explain: -तम is the ending of the superlative: भिषक् + तमम् = the best physician.
questions.teaches: -तम added to a word means 'the most ...': भिषक्तम = the most physician-like, the best physician.
questions.rule: भिषक् + तम = best physician.

questions.q: Which is the right split of सिद्धिराख्याति?
optionExplain: राख्याति is not a word.
Right: A visarga before a vowel becomes र्, so सिद्धिः + आख्याति is written सिद्धिराख्याति.
The verb is आख्याति, with आ.
That would give सिद्ध्याख्याति.
questions.explain: सिद्धिराख्याति = सिद्धिः + आख्याति.
questions.rule: सिद्धिः + आख्याति → सिद्धिराख्याति.

questions.q: A physician's procedures, done correctly, lead to success again and again. By verse 135, what does that success do?
options: It makes his procedures correct afterwards
It proves he took money from patients
It proclaims the correct application of his procedures
It shows that no medicine was needed
optionExplain: Success proclaims; it does not cause the correctness.
135 says nothing about money.
Right: सिद्धिः आख्याति सम्यक्प्रयोगम्.
Nothing like this is said.
questions.explain: Success shows that the application was correct.
