questions.rule: सिद्धि shows सम्यक्प्रयोग.

questions.q: A new line reads समृद्धिर्गृहस्थस्य यत्नमाख्याति (invented). By the same sense of आख्याति, what does the prosperity do?
optionExplain: आख्याति means to proclaim, not to hide.
The effect proclaims the cause, not the reverse.
Nothing about ending is said.
Right: आख्याति = proclaims, shows: the result speaks for what lies behind it.
questions.explain: A result can 'proclaim' its cause, as success proclaims correct practice.
questions.rule: result + आख्याति + cause = the result shows the cause.
questions.teaches: You can read a result-word as a witness to its cause whenever आख्याति joins them.

questions.q: Verse 136 has no verb, only a string of nouns. What kind of passage is it?
options: A list of topics whose closing statement comes later
An order given to the student
optionExplain: Right: Nouns without a verb are items of a list; the closing statement is in verse 140.
No person or event is narrated.
There is no verb of command.
No god is addressed.
questions.explain: A run of nouns with no verb is a list; look ahead for what completes it.
questions.rule: A verbless run of nouns = list of topics.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the five topics.
questions.rule: आगमः = coming; प्रवर्तनम् = propagation; अभ्यनुज्ञानम् = approval; निर्णयः = definition.

questions.q: आयुर्वेदागमः = आयुर्वेद + ____ (type the second word, 'coming', in Devanagari).
questions.explain: आगमः is the second member.
questions.teaches: आयुर्वेद + आगमः: अ + आ → आ, giving आयुर्वेदागमः (and the visarga becomes ओ before the voiced ह of हेतुः).
questions.rule: आयुर्वेदागमः = आयुर्वेद + आगमः.

questions.q: आगमस्य can carry two senses. Which two?
optionExplain: Departure is not a sense of आगम.
Right: आगम means both: 'coming' and the teaching that came down.
आगम does not mean the student.
Those are हेतु and कार्य, different words.
questions.explain: आगम = what has come: both the arrival and the teaching received.
questions.rule: आगम = arrival / received teaching.

questions.q: Put the five topics in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Coming, cause, propagation, approval of composition, definition.
questions.rule: आगम → हेतु → प्रवर्तन → अभ्यनुज्ञान → निर्णय.

questions.q: A teacher announces: विषयाः शब्दः, अर्थः, प्रयोगः, निर्णयः (invented). What is this line?
options: A complete command to the class
A list of topics (nouns with no verb)
optionExplain: There is no verb, so there is no command.
The items are separate words.
Right: Nouns in a row without a verb are a list, as in 136.
Nothing here is a question.
questions.explain: As in 136 → 140, read a verbless row of nouns as a list and look for a summing-up line, if any.
questions.rule: Verbless nouns in a row = a list.
questions.teaches: When you meet a row of naming-form nouns with no verb, treat it as a list of topics and look ahead for a sentence that sums it up, if there is one.

questions.q: Which item of verse 137 names the purpose of Āyurveda?
optionExplain: दोषाः are the doṣas.
भेषजम् is medicine.
हेतवः are causes (of disease).
Right: प्रयोजनम् means 'purpose'; the compound is 'purpose of Āyurveda'.
questions.explain: आयुर्वेदप्रयोजनम् = the purpose of Āyurveda.
questions.rule: प्रयोजनम् = purpose.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the items of the list.
questions.rule: कारणम् = cause; कार्यम् = effect; दोषाः = doṣas; भेषजम् = medicine.

questions.q: In हेतवश्चैव the small emphatic word after च is ____ (type it in Devanagari; it means indeed, alone).
questions.explain: हेतवश्चैव = हेतवः + च + एव.
questions.teaches: च + एव joins into चैव (अ + ए → ऐ), and the visarga of हेतवः becomes श् before च.
questions.rule: हेतवश्चैव = हेतवः + च + एव.

questions.q: 136 had हेतुः and 137 has हेतवः. How do they differ?
options: हेतुः is singular 'the cause'; हेतवः is plural 'causes'
हेतुः is plural; हेतवः is singular
हेतुः is dual; हेतवः is singular
optionExplain: Right: Both are the naming form of the same noun; only the number differs.
It is the other way round.
Neither is dual.
They are one noun in two numbers.
questions.explain: हेतुः (136) is the one cause; हेतवः (137) are causes.
questions.rule: -उः singular / -अवः plural for words like हेतु.

questions.q: Which are named in the second line of verse 137?
optionExplain: Right: the causes.
रसाः belongs to the next verse.
Right: the doṣas.
कारणम् is in the first line.
Right: medicine.
questions.explain: Line 2: हेतवः, दोषाः, भेषजम् and then संग्रहेण (in brief).
questions.rule: Line 2 names causes, doṣas, medicine.

questions.q: A new line joins two words with च: पुत्रः + च. How is it written as one word?
optionExplain: The visarga does not simply vanish before च.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्, as in हेतवः + च → हेतवश्च.
ओ appears before voiced sounds, not before च.
स् appears before त्, not before च.
questions.explain: Visarga + च → श्च, the same rule as हेतवश्च and दोषाश्च.
questions.rule: visarga + च → श्च.
questions.teaches: You can join any word ending in a visarga with च by changing the visarga to श्.

questions.q: Which of these is named in verse 138?
optionExplain: क्षीराणि comes in the next verse.
मूत्रम् comes in the next verse.
Right: मूलिन्यः is in the second line.
That comes at the very end, in verse 140.
questions.explain: 138 names tastes, classes of substances, root-plants, fruit-plants, fats and salts.
questions.rule: 138 includes मूलिन्यः.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the topics named.
questions.rule: रसाः = tastes; मूलिन्यः = root-plants; फलिन्यः = fruit-plants; स्नेहाः = fats.

questions.q: The verse speaks of a ____-fold classification of substances, त्रिविधः (type the number).
questions.explain: त्रि- means three.
questions.teaches: त्रिविधः = three kinds; the verse says the classification is threefold but does not list the three here.
questions.rule: त्रिविध = threefold.

questions.q: In सप्रत्ययद्रव्याः, what does the opening स- add?
options: 'Together with': the tastes with their underlying substances
optionExplain: स- does not mean 'without'.
The count 'six' would be षष्-.
'Not' would be अ-.
Right: स- here means 'with', giving 'with their underlying substances'.
questions.explain: सप्रत्ययद्रव्याः = tastes together with their underlying substances.
questions.rule: स- = with.

questions.q: Put the four plant and substance classes in the order of the second line.
questions.explain: Root-plants, fruit-plants, fats, salts.
questions.rule: मूलिनी → फलिनी → स्नेह → लवण.

questions.q: In a new line, सपत्रा लता (invented) is used of a creeper. How do you read सपत्रा?
options: With leaves, as in the form 'स- = with'
optionExplain: Right: सपत्रा = स + पत्रा, built like सप्रत्यय-: it means 'having leaves'.
That would need अ- or निः-.
स- is not the number six.
Nothing suggests salt.
questions.explain: स- + noun = 'having / together with' that noun.
questions.rule: स + X = together with X.
questions.teaches: The opening स- turns a noun into 'together with it', so you can read new words like सपत्र.

questions.q: By which useful parts does verse 139 describe the six trees?
optionExplain: Those belong to the plants of verse 138 (मूलिनी, फलिनी).
Right: क्षीरत्वगाश्रयाः = those whose seat of use is latex and bark.
Leaves and flowers are not mentioned.
Wood and seed are not mentioned.
questions.explain: The six trees are defined by latex and bark.
questions.rule: षड् वृक्षाः = क्षीर + त्वक् as आश्रय.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the topics of the verse.
questions.rule: मूत्रम् = urine; क्षीराणि = milks; वृक्षाः = trees; कर्माणि = actions.

questions.q: In क्षीरत्वगाश्रयाः the word for 'bark' is ____ (type its base form in Devanagari).
questions.explain: त्वक् / त्वच् means bark (skin).
questions.teaches: क्षीर-त्वक्-आश्रयाः: the क् becomes ग् before the vowel आ, giving त्वगाश्रयाः.
questions.rule: त्वक् = bark.

questions.q: In the pair योग / अयोग, what does अयोग stand for?
optionExplain: That is योग itself.
Neither word names a medicine.
Right: अ- reverses योग, 'proper application', giving 'improper application'.
सिद्धि is the word for success (verse 135).
questions.explain: योग = proper use; अयोग = improper use.
questions.rule: अयोग = the reverse of योग.

questions.q: Which are named in verse 139?
optionExplain: Salts are in verse 138.
Right: urine.
Fats are in verse 138.
Right: the milks.
Right: the six trees.
questions.explain: Urine, milks and the six trees are in 139; salts and fats are in 138.
questions.rule: 139: मूत्र, क्षीर, वृक्ष; 138: स्नेह, लवण.

questions.q: Following the pair गुण / अगुण, what does a new word अलवण most likely mean?
optionExplain: अ- does not mean 'full of'.
अ- turns the sense to its opposite.
Nothing in the word suggests fruit.
Right: अ- reverses or negates, so अलवण = without salt.
questions.explain: अ- + word = the opposite or lack of it.
questions.rule: अ + X = not X.
questions.teaches: The negative अ- before a consonant lets you read a new word like अलवण from the word it reverses.

questions.q: How does verse 140 end the list that began in verse 136?
options: It says that all this has been fully explained in the earlier ('first') chapter
It adds a new list of diseases
It asks the sages to explain more
It names the writer of the chapter
optionExplain: Right: सर्वमेतत् समाख्यातं पूर्वाध्याये = all this has been fully explained in the earlier ('first') chapter.
It closes the list; it adds none.
Nothing is asked.
The sage is called only महर्षिणा, 'by the great sage', not named.
questions.explain: The closing sentence sums the list up: सर्वमेतत् समाख्यातम्.
questions.rule: 140 closes the list with a summary sentence.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The key words of the closing verse.
questions.rule: वैद्यापवादः = censure of physicians; गुणाः = qualities; समाख्यातम् = fully explained; महर्षिणा = by the great sage.

questions.q: वैद्यापवादः = वैद्य + ____ (type the second word, meaning 'censure', in Devanagari).
questions.explain: अपवादः is 'censure'.
questions.teaches: वैद्य + अपवादः: अ + अ → आ, giving वैद्यापवादः; the visarga becomes ओ before the voiced य of यत्रस्थाः.
questions.rule: वैद्यापवादः = वैद्य + अपवादः.

questions.q: What does the verse itself say about the 'great sage'?
options: He is called only the great sage; no personal name is given here
optionExplain: Indra is not mentioned in 140.
Right: The verse says महर्षिणा and nothing more.
Bharadvāja is not mentioned in 140.
महर्षिणा is singular.
questions.explain: The sage is unnamed in this verse.
questions.rule: महर्षिणा = by the great sage (unnamed).

questions.q: समाख्यातम् is a past participle. What does it tell you about the topics of the list?
options: They are being asked about now
optionExplain: That would need a future form.
Nothing here is a question.
Right: A past participle states a finished action: 'has been explained'.
Nothing here forbids it.
questions.explain: समाख्यातम् = has been fully explained: the topics are already covered.
questions.rule: Past participle = a finished action.

questions.q: A new text lists topics and closes सर्वमेतद् उक्तं द्वितीयेऽध्याये (invented). What does the ending tell you?
options: They will be treated in a later chapter
The listed topics were treated in the second chapter
optionExplain: उक्तम् is a past participle: already said.
Nothing in the ending says so.
The list has just named them.
Right: As in 140, the closing line points back to where the listed topics were dealt with.
questions.explain: A closing 'all this has been said in chapter X' sends you back to that chapter.
questions.rule: सर्वमेतत् ... उक्तम्/समाख्यातम् + chapter = the summary points back.
questions.teaches: When a list ends with 'all this was said in chapter X', treat it as a table of contents pointing back.
